answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before it can submit jobs, and the protocol slashes that deposit when a randomly audited job fails a verifiable quality test. A hollow profile earns no trust merely by multiplying identities: every new identity needs fresh capital, while coordinated low-quality submissions risk losing it. A lantern audit samples work unpredictably, so attackers cannot cheaply target only known checks; the lotus of many fake accounts becomes expensive to maintain and easy to prune.
